question: The western Mediterranean multiannual fisheries plan will further reduce the number of fishing days in 2026, resulting in months of great uncertainty for the Italian bottom trawling industry.

Early indications suggest that the EU could either keep up the pace of fishing effort cuts or even increase it by as much as 40 %, potentially resulting in many fleets in the Tyrrhenian, Ionian, Ligurian and Adriatic Seas not going out to sea at all until January 2026.

Industry associations complain that the current system does not differentiate according to geographical area or fleet size and penalises both artisanal fisheries and territories with tougher operating conditions.

In addition, several scientific studies and data sets indicate that, while the multiannual plan has had dire socioeconomic repercussions for coastal communities, it has not fully achieved its environmental objectives. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission not agree that it should drastically revise the criteria used by the fishing effort reduction plan and that, at the very least, it should provide exemptions from them based on fairer parameters which take local conditions into account?
If the Commission does not agree, does it not think that it should at least enact extraordinary financial support measures for the businesses and fleets affected?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.1.2026) Some Mediterranean stakeholders advocated that a tailored1 management approach, informed by robust and detailed disaggregated datasets, can enhance precision in decision-making and the alignment of management with conservation, social and economic objectives.

The Commission explored a more disaggregated approach for the implementation of the Western Mediterranean Multi-Annual Management Plan (MAP), following the repartition of the Geographical sub-Areas (GSAs)2.

In 2025, the Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries indicated3 differences in the status of each stock group and therefore considered that the fishing mortality needs to be reduced differently between the stock groups and GSAs.

Considering that the most vulnerable stock in each Effort Management Unit is not present in all GSAs, the Commission proposed to compensate, in the respective GSAs, fishing vessels not fishing the most vulnerable stock.

This was meant to ensure a level-playing field between the fleets of different GSAs, as reflected in the Commission non paper on the Western Mediterranean Fishing Opportunities4, complementing the original Commission proposal.

Τhe European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) can support a wide range of actions for Member States to implement with their national EMFAF programmes, including temporary and permanent cessation measures in order to achieve the objectives of the Western Mediterranean MAP, insurance schemes, actions for selectivity improvement, reduction of undersize catches and efficient closure areas as well as actions to support the resilience of the sector and advancing on its innovation and energy transition.
